text: Every AI app I try asks me the same things. What I eat. Where I fly from.
Satchel is one memory that all my AI apps share. I say it once, I pick which apps may read it, and one tap takes it back.
Pip is the first app. I create my vault with my passkey, the fingerprint or face unlock my phone already uses.
I tell Pip I'm vegetarian. Pip saves it in my browser, locked so only apps I allow can open it.
Then: I fly out of B L R. Same thing.
cap: Then: I fly out of BLR. Same thing.

text: What gets stored is scrambled. No app reads it without my yes.
Now Fern, a different AI app. It sees nothing about me.
Fern asks for access, and Pip asks me. Saying yes costs a tiny network fee, so I add a little.
Allow. That writes a grant to Monad, a public network anyone can check: a permission slip any app can check and no app can fake.
Only the permission slip goes on the public record. The memories themselves stay locked in my browser.
Fern opens both memories with its own key. It never touched my passkey.
I ask it to plan my weekend. Vegetarian food, a flight out of B L R. It never asks me a thing.
cap: I ask it to plan my weekend. Vegetarian food, a flight out of BLR. It never asks me a thing.

text: Now I change my mind. I tap ree-voke Fern.
cap: Now I change my mind. I tap Revoke Fern.

text: Pip relocks every memory with a new lock. Fern's permission is cancelled.
I go back to Fern and ask again.
Every memory is locked. The plan comes back generic. Fern didn't promise to forget. It can't open my memories any more.
Straight from Monad's public record: Fern's permission reads cancelled, and the lock is on version two.
For developers it's one install: lock, grant, take back. The code on the page is the code that runs.
My AI's memory follows me to any app I allow, and one tap takes it back. Try satchel at satchel dash keys dot ver cell dot app.
